questions.stem: The Preamble of the Indian Constitution declares India to be a sovereign, socialist, secular, democratic:
questions.explanation: Republic — the head of state (President) is elected, not hereditary. 'Socialist' and 'secular' were inserted by the 42nd Amendment (1976).
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The Right to Education was added to the Constitution as Article 21-A by which amendment?
questions.explanation: 86th Amendment (2002) inserted Art 21-A making free + compulsory education for children aged 6-14 a fundamental right. RTE Act 2009 operationalised it from 1 April 2010.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT a Constitutional Body in India?
questions.explanation: NCW is a STATUTORY body set up under the National Commission for Women Act 1990 — not a constitutional body. ECI (Art 324), UPSC (Art 315), FC (Art 280) are constitutional. NCW, NHRC, NCPCR are statutory.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: How many Schedules does the Indian Constitution currently have?
questions.explanation: Currently 12 schedules. The original Constitution had 8. New additions: 9th (1951) — land-reform protection; 10th (1985) — anti-defection; 11th (1992) — 73rd Amendment, Panchayats; 12th (1992) — 74th Amendment, Municipalities.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: Consider the following about the SUPREME COURT of India. 1. It was inaugurated on 28 January 1950. 2. The sanctioned strength of judges (as of 2024) is 34 including the CJI. 3. Art. 143 permits the President to seek the Supreme Court's advisory opinion (advisory jurisdiction). 4. Supreme Court judges hold office until 62 years of age. Which are correct?
questions.explanation: Statement 4 is WRONG — Supreme Court judges retire at 65 (High Court judges retire at 62). The strength 34 was set by the Supreme Court (Number of Judges) Amendment Act, 2019. SC inaugurated in the Chamber of Princes, Parliament House, Jan 28, 1950.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The FIRST Indian state to be formed on linguistic basis was:
questions.explanation: Andhra state carved out of Madras on 1 Oct 1953 after Potti Sriramulu's hunger-strike (death 15 Dec 1952). Renamed Andhra Pradesh in 1956 post States Reorganisation Act. Maharashtra + Gujarat came in 1960.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: The Directive Principles of State Policy are contained in which Part of the Constitution?
questions.explanation: Part IV (Arts. 36-51). Part III = Fundamental Rights; Part IV-A = Fundamental Duties (added 42nd Amendment); Part V = Union. Article 37 itself declares DPSPs non-justiciable but 'fundamental in the governance'.
questions.subject: Polity

questions.stem: ASSERTION (A): The Vice-President of India is elected by members of both Houses of Parliament — NOT by State Legislatures. REASON (R): The VP's role is primarily federal (as ex-officio Chairman of Rajya Sabha), not state-level, which is why states don't vote.

options.option_text: Both A and R are true, R is the correct explanation
Both A and R are true, R is NOT the correct explanation
A is true, R is false
A is false, R is true

questions.explanation: Unlike the President (elected by MPs + MLAs), the VP is elected by MPs (both elected + nominated). Rationale: the VP's constitutional role is presiding over the RS (federal chamber), so only national legislators vote. R gives the structural reason for A.
